senses.gloss:
sīmantonnayana
(‘parting of the hair [of a pregnant woman] upwards’)
------------------------------------------
This is the third of the sixteen सṁस्कारस्, generally known as षोडश-सṁस्कारस्. It is a ritual act performed on a pregnant woman by her husband to protect the baby in the womb from evil spirits and confer a long life on it.
The earliest reference to it is in the Mantra Brāhmaṇa (1.5.2) of the Sāma-veda. Several गृह्यसूत्रस् also deal with it in greater detail.
The rite is to be performed during the fourth or the fifth month of pregnancy.
Since it is considered a purificatory rite of the मोथेर्, it is enough if it is performed during the first pregnancy only.
The following are the steps of the rite: Mātṛkāpūjana (worship of the seven मोथेर्-goddesses like ब्राह्मी, Māheśvarī etc.); Nāndīśrāddha; oblations to प्रजापति; parting of the hair of the pregnant woman upwards by her husband using a bunch of unripe udumbara (fig tree) fruits, दर्भ-grass (Poa cynosuroides) and porcupines quill and a stick of vīratara wood (or बिल्व); playing on a lute and so on.
Then some duties were prescribed for the pregnant woman and her husband. They were aimed at protecting her from evil influences and over-exertion. Others were calculated to preserve her physical and mental health. The husband was advised to fulfil all her wishes, as also avoid taking part in rituals or processions connected with death and śrāddha.
See also ṢOḌAŚASAṀSKĀRAS.
